coverage.explanation: Wrapper-enforced: retainRegistration admits current-head replay only when tx.head(source) equals registrationDigest(e) and exact() then requires uncached tx.read(digest) to snapshot-equal e (lines 44 and 30-34). A non-matching head must equal e.previous or deny (line 45), which rejects stale replay of an older envelope once a newer head exists (test lines 75-77). Gaps are rejected by old.sequence+1===e.sequence (lines 46-50; sequence 3 counterexample in the bad-envelope loop at lines 72-73). Mismatched predecessors are rejected by previous CAS, registrationDigest(old)===e.previous, old.source===e.source, and missing tx.read(previous) (undefined fails snapshot/deny; ungated test lines 80-81). Changed durable readback is denied before any source call (transport capture with mutated recoveryEvidence on read, called===0, lines 82-86). Append-once of the visible head is wrapper-level CAS plus skip-append on digest match; load-length===1 after idempotent retain is a fixture assertion, not a storage proof. Crash-durable append-only compare-and-append and true uncached head reads are delegated to withAuthority/tx, not implemented in the wrapper. Native two-phase putOnce(envelope) then putOnce(sequence-index) with an injected failure before index (incarnationCases 137-149) shows an unpublished head can be retried for the same envelope; that is adapter crash-window behavior, not a second wrapper-level head.

coverage.explanation: Independently configured head is a constructor argument: createCustodyBoundTransport denies unless expectedHead===registrationDigest(e) (line 59) and later exact() requires tx.head(e.source) to equal that same digest (lines 67, 32). Identity is frozen from the envelope at construction (registrationEnvelope, scope(), inner createIncarnationBoundTransport({incarnationId:e.incarnationId})). Capture/prepare synchronously deny other bindingId/source/stream before withAuthority (lines 63-65); tests throw on binding/source/stream mismatch with calls===0 (lines 91-95). Advance carries no source/stream/binding fields; continuity is via exact() plus retained requestScope. Cross-sequence retainRegistration requires new bindingId and new incarnationId and same source, but does not require old.stream===e.stream (lines 46-50): stream retarget on recovery is accepted at chain level and only re-pinned when a new transport is constructed. Documented scope is synthetic/qualification-only, no production custodian or protected head (docs lines 3,15; registrationCustody.mjs line 1). Native cross-scope acceptance: the custody test uses a separate runtime/key but the same physical PostgreSQL restore domain as the source (incarnationCases comments 119-120); that is documented fixture integration, not an independent custody boundary. Automatic source pins are rejected as envelope malformations (source:'auto', extra auto:true).

findings.description: Filesystem fixture overrides tx.read and tx.readRequest to load durable bytes, but tx.head continues to use the callback-local in-memory rows snapshot (plus in-callback rows.push). exact() therefore compares a memory head to a disk body. Docs/comments claim independent durable reads; head is not included.
findings.counterexample: Inside fixture withAuthority, head is rows.filter(...).at(-1)?.digest while read is (await load()).find(...). A fixture that rows.push without a matching durable last line, or a durable extra registration line not reflected in rows, would not be caught by the same head-from-disk check the wrapper comments require the adapter to provide.
findings.remediation: Point fixture tx.head at an uncached load of durable bytes (last registration digest per source) without using this finding as production design.

findings.description: Registration chaining pins source, predecessor digest, sequence+1, and inequality of bindingId/incarnationId, but does not require old.stream to equal e.stream. Stream identity is per constructed transport, not per source chain.
findings.counterexample: After a valid sequence-1 retain, a sequence-2 envelope with previous=digest(first), new bindingId, new incarnationId, and a different stream UUID satisfies retainRegistration (lines 46-50) and becomes current head.
findings.remediation: If recovery must preserve stream epoch, deny old.stream!==e.stream in the sequence>1 predecessor check and add that counterexample to tests.

Worker run 34832064845 job 103937438592 ran the new native custody test on merge e75c2e2 whose tree matches the candidate; that is fixture integration against the existing encrypted journal and incarnation RPCs, including unpublished-index retry and old-path closure without rewriting source_incarnations, not independent custody or certification. I distinguish those wrapper checks from trusted-adapter assumptions (auth, exclusion, durable CAS, uncached head) and from missing journal/SQL/golden-log evidence recorded as blockers.
